newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Netanyahu to meet Arafat on Tuesday over Hebron.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu to meet Arafat on Tuesday over Hebron.

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat will meet Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Tuesday to finalise a deal on the handover of the West Bank town of Hebron to PLO rule, an aide to Arafat said on Monday.
"Prime Minister Netanyahu and President Arafat will meet on Tuesday at 11 a.m. (0900 GMT) at Erez to finalise an agreement on Hebron," Nabil Abu Rdainah said.
Any agreement on Hebron is likely to breathe new life into an Arab-Israeli peace process on the brink of collapse.
"The summit will be a step towards concluding the Hebron agreement. Some issues were left to be finalised by the two leaders," Abu Rdainah said.
He said Netanyahu and Arafat will meet at the Erez crossing between Israel and the Palestinian-ruled Gaza Strip.

Israeli and Palestinian negotiators joined by U.S. Middle East envoy Dennis Ross continued their talks in Jerusalem late on Monday in an effort to create a draft agreement, said a PLO official who did not want to be identified.
The official said if the outstanding issues were resolved, an agreement would be announced by the two leaders and the Israeli troop redeployment from 80 percent of Hebron would begin within hours.
Israeli and Palestinian negotiators said on Monday that progress had been made in the discussions to break a deadlock over Hebron by Christmas.
Ross has shuttled between Israel, PLO-ruled Gaza and Egypt since his arrival on Saturday to try and clinch a deal on an Israeli troop redeployment in the town.
Arafat and Netanyahu met in Washington in October in another U.S.-brokered effort to push the stalled peace process forward.
